# SceneTemplate

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.SceneBuilding` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/SceneBuilder/Scene/SceneTemplate.cs#L22)

A reusable scene setup: a captured scene, an ordered list of installers, and any prefabs
that come with them. All three are optional, so a template can be a whole scene, a bare
recipe of framework modules, or both.
Applying one is never a one-off. A template can be applied to any scene, as often as you
like - each installer tops up what is missing and leaves what is already there alone - and a
template itself is a lasting thing you can author, save and hand to someone else, either as
a [`VRFSceneTemplateAsset`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-scenebuilding/VRFSceneTemplateAsset) in the project or as a subclass of this in an editor
script.

### IsFullyApplied {#isfullyapplied}

True when every installer in the template is already satisfied. Reported on the card as
information only - it never stops the template being applied again.
A template carrying a scene is never "applied": its objects are copies, so bringing them
in again is a real thing to do rather than a no-op, and saying otherwise would be a lie.


## Methods

### Apply() {#apply}

Merges in the template's scene, runs every installer that is not already satisfied, then
drops in the template's prefabs. Safe to run on a scene that already has some of the
template in it, and safe to run twice - though a second run brings a second copy of the
scene's objects, which is the honest meaning of merging a scene twice.

```csharp
public virtual void Apply()
```

[View source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/SceneBuilder/Scene/SceneTemplate.cs#L82)

### Replace() {#replace}

Wipes the active scene and applies the template to the empty result. Destructive - the
caller is responsible for confirming with the user first.
This deliberately keeps you in your own scene file rather than opening the template's
scene, so a save cannot overwrite the template. The cost is that scene level settings -
lighting, skybox, fog - stay yours; see `MergeScene()`.

```csharp
public void Replace()
```
